This article lists keyboard shortcuts in Mozilla Firefox.{for linux} The shortcuts only work if they are not used by the desktop environment or window manager.{/for}{for linux} If you have enabled Emacs-style text editing shortcuts in GNOME, they will also work in Firefox. When an Emacs text editing shortcut conflicts with the default shortcuts (as occurs with {key Ctrl}+{key K}), the Emacs shortcut will take precedence if focus is inside a text box (which would include the address bar and search bar). In such cases you should use the alternate keyboard shortcut if one is listed below.{/for}
*For mouse shortcuts, see [[Use mouse shortcuts to perform common tasks in Firefox]].
*To customize shortcuts, see [[Customize keyboard shortcuts in Firefox]].

=Selection of Multiple Tabs=
{note}These shortcuts require the tab bar to be “in focus”. Currently, the only way to do this is to focus an adjacent object and “tab into” the tab bar, for instance, by hitting {for win,linux}{key Ctrl+L}{/for}{for mac}{key command+L}{/for} to focus the address bar, and then {key Shift+Tab} repeatedly until the current tab gets a colored border.{/note}
{|
!'''Command'''
!'''Shortcut'''
|-
|Select left, right, first or last tab. Deselect all other tabs.
|Arrow Keys<br>{key Home}<br>{key End}
|-
|Move the colored border to left, right, first or last tab.
|{for win,linux}{key Ctrl}{/for}{for mac}{key command}{/for} + Arrow&nbsp;Keys<br>{for win,linux}{key Ctrl}{/for}{for mac}{key command}{/for} + {key Home}<br>{for win,linux}{key Ctrl}{/for}{for mac}{key command}{/for} + {key End}
|-
|Select or deselect the tab with the colored border. The other tabs stay selected or deselected.
|{for win,linux}{key Ctrl+Space}{/for}{for mac}{key command+space}{/for}
|}

=Developer shortcuts=
You can also use keyboard shortcuts with developer tools in Firefox. See the [https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/keyboard_shortcuts/index.html All keyboard shortcuts] ''Firefox Source Docs'' page.
